paragraphs: Rabbi Ammi the priest. (a) Chullin 107b. Hazeroa (Chullin 134b): Rabbi Ammi took priority when a purse of dinars arrived at the academy. One explanation is that he acquired it for the poor. An alternative appeals to his standing, which Rashi explains as the standing of an academy head. Rashi identifies the original recipients as the academy’s students. Ellu Metzi'ot 28b: Rabbi Ammi found a vessel of dinars. When he saw that a Roman was afraid, Ammi told him to take it, saying, “We are not like Persians.” The scholars report that Ammi wrote four hundred Torah scrolls. Rav Hamnuna suggests he may have copied the seven-word “Moses commanded us Torah” passage. Heilprin relates those seven words to the seven books. See Bava Batra 14a. He busied himself with matters and saw a raven abandon its white young; three days later their excrement bred gnats they ate, becoming black. “To the raven’s young that cry,” or “Who prepares the raven’s prey?” Heilprin cites Midrash Shmuel. The checked Midrash Shmuel names Rav Assi in this episode. Metzora Rabbah, beginning of section 19, instead has Rabbi Assi and a different account; see Rashi, Ketubbot 49b. Tosafot on Ketubbot, citing Chullin, distinguishes a white raven from a black one and identifies the valley raven as white. Yuchasin’s gloss: a place in India has white ravens.

(b) His colleague Rabbi Assi the priest, Tosafot, Kirah 45b: distinguished priests in the Land, Megillah 22, end of a; Sotah 38b. The Land’s judges (see there), empowered to extract money and make a prosbul. Chisda judged in Babylonia then. Chisda’s decision reached Rabbi Ammi, who said, etc.; they returned it to Chisda, who said, etc.; they returned it to Rabbi Ammi, etc., Bava Metzia 40a. Rav Chisda called Rabbi Ammi a great man, Yevamot 21b. At Rabbi Ammi and Rabbi Assi’s ordination they sang, “Ordain such men for us,” etc., Ketubbot 17a; Sanhedrin, chapter 1. They carried Sabbath utensils on their shoulders, going in and out, Shabbat 119a. Three “one says, the other says” matters, Yoma 74, end of b. Bava Metzia 24, end of b: Rabbi Ammi came before Rabbi Assi. Tosafot: though listed first and greater, he consulted his colleague. Reading Abba instead is difficult, Abba being Rabbi Ammi’s student: how could he always come before him? End quotation. Tosafot, Bava Batra 33b [Heilprin cites 34a]: Rabbi Assi’s “My teacher, you say so; Rabbi Yochanan said thus,” Gittin 54b, still addresses a colleague, called teacher for greater standing. Shevuot 47a likewise: Rabbi Ammi sought advice; alternatively, later Rabbi Ammi was head, with judges coming before him. They prayed between pillars, Berakhot 8a; submitted to Rav Huna (see Rabbi Assi). Rabbi Yochanan’s students; Rabbi Ammi was his outstanding student and successor as academy head in Tiberias, Kol Habbasar 111b. Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot 2, mishnah 3: “Rabbi Ammi Asya said, Yirmeyah ruled beyond him.” One reading: Rabbi Ammi says Rabbi Assi, meaning Rav Assi, ruled—what? Yirmeyah, etc. Another: Rabbi Ammi was a physician, Sedeh Yehoshua; see Rav Assi. Gittin 40a: Rabbi Ammi and Rabbi Assi spoke before him. Heilprin’s Hebrew has Yochani [יוחני]. The checked Rashi says “before Rabbi Yochanan.” Heilprin contrasts him with Rav Dimi, treated as their junior in Responsa B.L., 161a [ב״ל; work unresolved]. Rabbi sent Rabbi Ammi and Rabbi Assi to set the Land in order, Eikhah Rabbah.
